lessons.title: Indices and the order of operations

objectives: Calculate with powers, including square brackets

teach.heading: Roots of fractions
bullets: Root the top and the bottom

lessons.title: Estimating calculations
lessons.bigQuestion: How do engineers check a calculation before trusting it with real lives?
objectives: Round to 1 significant figure to estimate
Estimate calculations including powers and roots
Judge whether an estimate is an over- or underestimate
successCriteria: Estimate products and quotients by rounding to 1 s.f.
Estimate calculations with roots, powers and fractions
Justify whether the estimate is too big or too small

lessons.smsc: Moral: responsibility to check work that affects other people

an approximate answer using rounded values
approximately equal to
an estimate smaller than the exact answer

teach.heading: Rounding roots
bullets: Round to a nearby square or cube
teach.note: Better to choose a perfect square than to round to 1 s.f. first: √47 rounded to √50 is no easier.

teach.heading: Over or under?
bullets: Numbers in the top rounded up: overestimate
Numbers in the bottom rounded up: underestimate
teach.note: In the model we rounded 9.87 up (over), √62 up (over), and 0.198 up in the bottom (under). The effects partly cancel.

check.why: 4³ = 64 and √100 = 10, so 64 − 10 = 54. B forgets to subtract the root; C adds it instead; D cubes the wrong way (4 × 3 + 9).

independent: Extend: Estimate (21.7 × 3.08²) ÷ √(15.8). Say if it is over or under and why.
Stretch: The Earth is about 150 million km from the Sun and light travels about 300 000 km per second. Estimate how long sunlight takes to reach us in minutes.
exit: Is your estimate of 9.8 × 3.1 over or under?
lessons.homework: Estimate then calculate five calculations from science or geography homework, recording the percentage difference.
lessons.send: Support: list of square and cube numbers. Stretch: order-of-magnitude problems.

any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1

10 multiplied by itself, e.g. 10³ = 1000
a number written in full

n says how many places the digits move

teach.heading: Ordering

A × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ A < 10
one millionth of a metre, 10⁻⁶ m
a position after the decimal point

The perimeter P of a regular hexagon with side s

change the formula so a different variable is the subject
an operation that undoes another
